primitives.name: AWS Learning-to-Repo Action Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: # AWS Learning To Repo Actions This file converts learning areas into no-cost repo artifacts.
primitives.assumptions: No-cost repository artifacts, safe evidence validation, explicit exclusion of paid resources.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Learning conversion into structured, verifiable, and reproducible repository entries.

layer2.mapping: Maps learning conversion into a dual space where each learning objective (L) corresponds to a verifiable repository artifact (A). The mapping preserves safety constraints: L → A, ensuring no secrets and zero operational cost. This establishes a formal duality between knowledge acquisition and repository construction.
layer2.telemetry: Artifact validation success rate, secret detection failures, cost avoidance metrics.

primitives.name: AWS Decision-Engine Evaluation Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Convert any future live AWS idea into an AWS decision-engine evaluation first.
primitives.assumptions: All live ideas undergo preliminary evaluation before deployment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pre-deployment screening to prevent unauthorized resource consumption.

layer2.mapping: Encodes the protocol as a binary decision kernel K(x) ∈ {0,1}, where x represents a live idea. K(x)=1 indicates the idea requires evaluation; otherwise, it proceeds directly. This kernel maps to GSI through conformal prediction intervals for resource usage forecasts, and to GSE via state-transition logic that tracks evaluation status.
layer2.telemetry: Evaluation backlog depth, unauthorized deployment incidents, forecast accuracy of resource costs.

primitives.name: AWS Cost-Security Gatekeeper
primitives.verbatim_quote: - The artifact confirms no secrets and no paid resource use.
primitives.assumptions: Zero secret exposure and zero monetary cost in all repository artifacts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Binary security threshold enforcement on all generated artifacts.

layer2.mapping: Establishes an isomorphism between the set of secure, cost-free artifacts (S) and a subspace of all possible artifacts (A). The gatekeeper acts as a projection operator P: A → S, which projects any artifact onto the safe subspace. This aligns with GSI's Bayesian inference framework by treating security compliance as a probabilistic event, and with GSE's state-transition logic by defining a 'secure' state as an absorbing state.
layer2.telemetry: Security breach count, unauthorized charge volume, gatekeeper rejection rate.

The core challenge is converting uncertain, evolving AWS learning into deterministic, verifiable repository actions while preventing cost overruns and secret leaks. This is framed as a constrained optimization problem: maximize informative content of A subject to safety constraints C(A) = 0. The solution leverages three key dualities. First, the learning artifact duality maps knowledge discovery to repository construction. Second, the decision-engine duality separates live ideas into evaluatable and non-evaluatable categories. Third, the cost-security duality projects all artifacts onto a safe subspace. These dualities collapse the high-dimensional uncertainty of AWS adoption into a low-dimensional, verifiable feature space. Failure modes include: (1) Overlooking critical edge cases in the mapping; (2) Inadequate coverage of security gates leading to false positives/negatives; (3) Ignoring the retrocausal history of AWS patterns, causing outdated heuristics.
